slot.brief: Show a figure of a substrate with a bulky/unsymmetrical alkyl group; choose the correct halide + alkoxide combination for Williamson synthesis

stem: Which reactant pair is most suitable for preparing the ether shown in the figure by Williamson synthesis?

verdicts.working: The ether is ethyl tert-butyl ether. Williamson synthesis works best with the less hindered halide: bromoethane with sodium tert-butoxide gives the target by SN2.

working:
The ether is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$.
Use a primary halide for the $S_\text{N}2$ step: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CONa} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaBr}$.
A tertiary halide favours elimination rather than Williamson substitution.

Independent check: The ether is ethyl tert-butyl ether. Williamson synthesis works best with the less hindered halide: bromoethane with sodium tert-butoxide gives the target by SN2.
solution:
Williamson synthesis proceeds by an $S_N2$ reaction, so the alkyl halide should be primary and least hindered.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CONa} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaBr}$$
Thus, bromoethane and sodium tert-butoxide form the ether shown.
